headline: Executive order on marine protected areas, ocean and coastal zones set aside for protection, signed by President Clinton in 2000.
what_it_does: This executive order deals with marine protected areas, which are parts of the ocean, coasts, or Great Lakes set aside for some level of protection. Based on the title alone, it sets federal policy on how these areas are handled. No summary was provided, so the specific rules, agency duties, and limits are not described here.

who_it_affects.group: Federal agencies that manage ocean and coastal areas
who_it_affects.how: These agencies are likely the main ones directed by the order on how to handle marine protected areas.

who_it_affects.group: People who fish, boat, or work in coastal and ocean areas
who_it_affects.how: Activities in marine protected areas may be shaped by how the order is carried out, though the details are not given in the source.

when_it_takes_effect: Signed May 26, 2000. Executive orders usually take effect when signed.
